answer: In an agent economy trading vine cuttings, marble tiles, and ledge planters, each agent's voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities gives exactly the same total voting power as staking them under one identity. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital that cannot be spent or sold during the lock period.
